answer: Require every agent to keep a memory-hard proof of storage: it must hold a unique, randomly seeded dataset and answer random lookups from it within tight deadlines. Each identity sits on its own terrace of disk that cannot be shared, because the datasets differ per key. A farmer running clones has to buy storage for every one, and the audit grows like a vine, demanding deeper lookups as an identity earns more. Push a fleet far enough and it falls off a cost ledge.
